chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Isma'il ibn Jabir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man saw a woman entering the house of a group of people and leaving, so he inquired about her and was told, 'She is their slave, and her name is so-and-so.' He said to them, 'Marry me to so-and-so.' When they married him to her, they informed him that she was the slave of someone else. He said, 'She and her child belong to her master.' I said: Then he came to them and proposed to them that they marry him to their free daughters. They married him to them, and he believed they were free. After she gave birth, they informed him that she was a slave. He said, 'The child belongs to him (the husband), and they are liable for the value of the child to the master of the female slave.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the child of a slave woman married to a free man who believed she was free?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *al-waladu li-l-firash* (the child follows the bed) in the context of a free man marrying a slave woman under the mistaken belief of her freedom. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the child belongs to the husband due to his marital right, the wife's master is liable to compensate the husband for the child's value, as the husband's entitlement was predicated on the assumption of the wife's free status.
